## Audit method and interpretation

CSV rows are streamed independently. Headerless UNSW raw partition columns are assigned
positionally from the local feature dictionary and observed 49-field layout; verify this
mapping against acquired documentation before modeling. Duplicate fingerprints hash
parsed cells plus the exact header. Equal hashes are treated as exact duplicates,
subject to negligible SHA-256 collision risk. Distinct counts are exact up to 50,000
values per column; higher cardinality is reported as a lower bound. Near-constant means
the leading value is at least 99.9% of rows, checked only below that cap.

Non-finite detection recognizes common NaN/Inf tokens and numeric parsing. Numeric
ranges are observed extrema, not validity judgments. Name-based label, identifier, and
timestamp flags are heuristic signals, not confirmed leakage. File identity and
timestamps may expose source or time information; the audit does not decide whether they
are valid model inputs.

## Implications for Experimental Design

- **Random splitting:** avoid as the primary protocol where records may share sessions,
duplicate rows, days, or source identifiers. It can be a secondary baseline after group
leakage is assessed.
- **Source/file-aware splitting:** preserve CIC-IDS2017 member and CSE date-file
boundaries where schemas permit. Keep CSE files separate; file-level splits can evaluate
day/source change. The 20 February CSE file has a different schema and needs explicit
feature mapping.
- **Temporal splitting:** use timestamps for CIC/CSE and TON where parsing is reliable.
UNSW raw partitions expose positional Stime/Ltime; official splits do not expose direct
timestamps. Review JSON ranges before defining windows and do not select windows from
test outcomes.
- **Cross-dataset evaluation:** keep datasets and label/feature semantics separate.
Transfer is supplementary and requires explicit common-feature and label mappings; do
not concatenate schemas.
- **Leakage risks:** assess exact duplicates across same-schema files, file/date
identifiers, IP/flow identifiers, timestamp-derived fields, label-like values, and
official split overlap. Drop or group identifiers only under a documented protocol. Test
data must not fit preprocessing or thresholds.
- **Development vs generalization:** CIC-IDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 have multiple
source/date files that can support development and held-out-file/day evaluation after
duplicate, label, and schema checks. UNSW-NB15 has an official train/test pair; use its
training split for development and retain testing for final evaluation, while validating
the raw-partition feature mapping. TON_IoT's single public-mirror file has no verified
internal split provenance, so it is a development candidate only after split provenance
is resolved, not a standalone generalization set. Cross-dataset evaluation needs frozen
feature and label maps. This audit does not rank datasets.
